public_payload.normalized_proposition: There is near-zero chance Musk deploys a billion robots by the end of this decade, and not much higher next decade.

statement.excerpt: The chance Elon will get his billion robots out this decade is near zero. Not that much higher next decade.
statement.document_title: Why my p(doom) has risen, dramatically

from_speaker: Not that much higher next decade
our_interpretation: Read as a forecast that Musk's companies are very unlikely to deploy one billion physical robots by either stated deadline.
Interpret 'get ... out' as cumulative deployment into use, including internal use. Announced capacity, orders and prototypes alone do not qualify.
From the July 2025 post, 'this decade' ends on 2029-12-31 and 'next decade' ends on 2039-12-31. The horizon records the later deadline; each component must be assessed separately.
Assess the predicted deployment outcome. Marcus supplies no numerical probability for either phrase, and a single outcome cannot establish whether his probability estimate was calibrated.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable deployment records establish that fewer than one billion qualifying robots had been deployed by 2029-12-31 for the first component and by 2039-12-31 for the second. This supports the directional forecast, not a precise probability estimate.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records establish cumulative deployment of at least one billion qualifying robots by the relevant deadline. Deployment by 2029-12-31 contradicts both directional components; first reaching the threshold during the 2030s contradicts the second component.
